title: Dynamic analysis (DAST) in a staging environment

videos.script: Lesson 3 read linkbox's code. A static scanner sees every line, and it never sees the service run. {{code}} Some defects are not on any line. They are in what the running service answers. A header that is missing. A server that says its own name. {{response}} Dynamic analysis asks the running thing. It sends requests, the way a browser would, and it judges the answers. {{requests}} First you build a staging for one run. A private network, the image you just built, and a scanner beside it. All of it is made for the run and thrown away after. {{staging}} The scanner is ZAP, in its baseline mode, which only reads. It finds four things in linkbox. Three are real, and three headers fix them, with a test that keeps them fixed. The fourth is a false positive. You will decide that from the response itself, not from the scanner's word. {{verdict}} Then the scan goes into the nightly run. And you will see why the other kind of scan, the active one, is pointed only at your own staging, and never at anything else. {{nightly}}
